comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Mechanism observed (RED), not assumed

Reproduced with a synthetic sentinel in a controlled child environment. The raw form renders
the mapping; the bool-bound form renders a bool:

```
E  AssertionError: assert 'REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH' not in environ({'SHELL': ..., <SENTINEL>, ...})
E   +  where environ({...}) = os.environ
```
vs.
```
E  assert not True
```

pytest's bounded mapping repr truncates the MIDDLE, so head and tail entries render in full —
truncation is not mitigation.

## Why the existing guard did not catch it — pattern set, not population

`tests/unit/test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py` rglobs **all** of `tests/**`, so its
population already covers the offending file. Its detector (`_raw_env_audit`) matches only
env-**construction** shapes — `dict(os.environ)`, `os.environ.copy()`, `{**os.environ}` —
because its purpose is routing subprocess environments through `subprocess_env()`. An
assert-comparator reference constructs nothing, so this is a genuinely different shape it does
not cover, not a population gap. Same underlying hazard class (a raw `os.environ` reaching a
repr), third distinct route: fixture argument reprs (`test_fixture_env_repr_security.py`),
subprocess env dicts (`test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py`), and now assertion operands.

## Fix

1. `tests/unit/test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup_heldout.py` — membership bound to a bool before the
   assert. No other site touched; the safe `os.environ.get(...)` assertions listed in the
   description were verified unmodified.
2. New sibling oracle `tests/unit/test_environ_assert_repr_security.py`, pytest-resident (not a
   CI-only step, so it is portable per `project.portability`):
   - **AST audit** over `tests/**`: an `assert` whose test *or message* names `os.environ`
     itself is a finding; a reference CONSUMED as the receiver of an attribute access or a
     subscript (`os.environ.get("X")`, `os.environ["X"]`) is sanctioned, since only the
     retrieved value becomes an operand. That rule flags exactly one site tree-wide (`:232`)
     and zero of the safe forms — no churn sweep.
   - **Behavioural probe** anchored to the REAL site: the guard's shipped statements are
     extracted by AST from the live module (following the binding forward), executed in a
     subprocess pytest run with the seam var set plus a sentinel, at `--tb=long` and
     `--tb=short`. It asserts the sentinel is ABSENT from the output. A reworded assertion
     message cannot make it pass.
   - Detector unit tests both ways: five reintroduction shapes flagged, three value-scoped
     shapes sanctioned.

## RED -> GREEN -> mutation

- RED (before fix): 3 failed, 9 passed — audit reported `...heldout.py:232`; probe leaked the
  sentinel at BOTH traceback styles.
- GREEN (after fix): 12 passed. Target module still 47 passed alongside both sibling oracles.
- MUTATION (raw form reintroduced): back to 3 failed, 9 passed — audit reported `:233`, probe
  leaked at both styles again. Restored, green.

## caused_by

`94188e90c0d7114ac4787b37bc8ba34d6bc9c6e4` — "RP-04 S6: compose op-cert signer at startup"
(2026-08-18 08:18 UTC), which created the file and the leaking line together.

Date test applied, because three of four attributions today turned out to be unmet obligations
where the fix site was not the cause site. Here it is NOT an unmet obligation: the ambient-secret
policy already existed in the tree when the line landed — `aa41c2e45a` ("Limit fixture
environments to required keys", 08:04 UTC) is a confirmed **ancestor** of `94188e9`
(`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), by ~14 minutes. The obligation predated the commit, so the
cause site is the commit that wrote the line. Fair caveat: the pre-existing oracle guarded a
different route, so no mechanism could have caught it — that mechanical gap is what this change
closes. The later `48d4a4d4a9` (subprocess redaction, 2026-08-18 18:41 UTC) did not create the
obligation either; it widened a sibling route without reaching this shape.

## Gates

`make lint` PASS, `make typecheck` PASS (598 files),
`check_complexity_baseline.py --check` -> `active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`,
`check_wall_clock_asserts.py` clean.

No real secret was printed at any point; the sentinel is a synthetic constant.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## The fast gates do not guard this class — and the guard's population WAS widened

Recording this because it generalises past this one fix.

**The fast gates are blind here.** `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the complexity ratchet were
ALL green with the leaking assertion in the tree, both before and after. Nothing in the
commit-time gate chain can see this class: it is not a style violation, not a type error, and
not a complexity increase. Only the full suite catches it — and only because someone wrote an
oracle for it.

**Two independent hits in one session.** A second agent hit the identical failure class today on
an unrelated ticket (a plain `dict(os.environ)` in a held-out test), on a host that demonstrably
carries live Jira credentials and an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Different route, same hazard, same day,
no contact between the two. Two independent occurrences in one session is not coincidence — it
says the pattern is easy to write by reflex and that vigilance is not a control.

**What prevents the third occurrence.** This change did NOT only fix the single instance. The new
oracle carries an AST audit that walks `tests/**` — the whole tree, every file, on every suite
run — so the guarded population is now the entire test suite rather than the one site named in
this ticket. Any future `assert` that names `os.environ` itself, anywhere in `tests/`, fails the
build with a file:line. That widening is the durable part of the fix; the one-line edit at the
op-cert site is the smaller half.

Coverage of the hazard class is now three complementary oracles, each policing all of `tests/**`:

| route | oracle |
| --- | --- |
| fixture-argument reprs | `test_fixture_env_repr_security.py` |
| subprocess environment dicts | `test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py` |
| assertion operands | `test_environ_assert_repr_security.py` (this change) |

Remaining known gap, not closed here and not claimed to be: a raw environment reaching output by
some fourth route — e.g. an explicit `print`/`logging` call, or a `pytest.fail(str(os.environ))`.
Worth a ticket if a fourth instance appears; three oracles for three observed routes is the
evidence-proportionate stopping point today.

**Caveat on the guards' own limits.** All three are pytest-resident, so they only fire when the
suite runs. They are portable (no CI dependency), but they are a suite-time control, not a
commit-time one. Anyone wanting commit-time enforcement would need an entry in the
`scripts/check_*` chain; that was deliberately not added here, because the CI-only trigger of the
existing `check_wall_clock_asserts.py` step is exactly the portability shape
`project.portability` warns against.

comments.body:
## Close record

Closed `preexisting` — a latent defect that predated this work. The leaking line was born with
the file in `94188e9` and was never previously fixed, so nothing was reintroduced (`regression`
would be wrong) and the design was not at fault (`plan_defect` would be wrong). Latent is exact:
the environment only renders when that assertion FAILS.

`caused_by` -> `ultrashort-immoderate-seriema` (`6f14-21a7-d806-44b2`), the RP-04 S6 story whose
commit `94188e9` wrote both the file and the line.

**Duplicate-edge hazard reproduced (4th occurrence today).** Pre-close the ticket carried exactly
one hand-made `caused_by` edge; the close auto-ran blame and attached a SECOND edge to the SAME
target, leaving two entries sharing `6f14-21a7-d806-44b2`. Removed with
`rebar unlink <ticket> <target> caused_by`, which took exactly one and left the other standing;
verified one edge remains. This is the behaviour tracked as `ruling-magnific-bats`
(`10d0-c26c-bdbb-4b1f`), fix in review as Gerrit 1973.

Worth noting as evidence for that fix: the auto-blame independently landed on the SAME origin
commit this investigation reached by hand. Blame was not wrong here — it was redundant. The
defect is the duplicate edge, not the attribution.

Landed as Gerrit change 1972, merged `4ad2eb877c`. Gerrit rebased on submit, so the local commit
was a pre-rebase twin; content verified byte-identical between the twin and the merged commit
before resetting the feature worktree onto it. The shared main checkout was not touched.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem
A pytest assertion of the form

```python
assert "SOME_VAR" not in os.environ
```

renders the **entire environment** into the failure output, because pytest shows the right-hand
operand. If any ambient secret is present in that environment — an API key, a Jira token, a signing
key — it lands in the pytest report and therefore in CI logs.

This is not hypothetical. While implementing `illusory-patronal-giraffe` (op-cert credential
hardening, Gerrit 1944, merged) the first RED run of a new test did exactly this and dumped the
throwaway key it had set. The implementer fixed its own test by binding membership to a bool first,
so a failure can only ever render `True`/`False`:

```python
present = "SOME_VAR" in os.environ
assert not present
```

## Scope — one surviving instance, and it is in the wrong subsystem
A sweep of `tests/` found the dangerous form surviving in exactly one place:

- `tests/unit/test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup_heldout.py:232`
  `assert "REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH" not in os.environ`
  — with the comment "Prove the binding — not the env — is the key source."

That is the **op-cert startup path**, i.e. the subsystem whose whole purpose is handling a signing
key, and the test runs with `compose_signer` live. It is the single worst place in the tree for this
pattern to survive.

The other `os.environ` assertions found are SAFE and should not be churned: they use
`os.environ.get("X")`, which renders only the retrieved value, not the whole mapping
(`test_repo_isolation_guard.py:188`, `test_reconciler_core_seam_clean_heldout.py:232,234`,
`test_import_idempotency.py:151`, plus live-only files under `tests/external/`). Do not "fix" those.

## There is already precedent for caring about this
`tests/unit/test_fixture_env_repr_security.py` exists and is described as a *"Regression oracle for
ambient-secret exposure through pytest fixture reprs."* So the project already guards one vector for
exactly this hazard — a fixture's repr leaking ambient secrets — but not the assertion vector. The
gap is narrow and the intent is clearly established; this ticket closes the other half.

## Sizing this honestly
The probability is low: the leak only occurs when that specific assertion FAILS. The impact is
high and durable: CI logs persist, are broadly readable, and a leaked signing key is not
recoverable by deleting the log. Cheap to fix, worth a guard so it does not reappear.

## Scope
1. Fix the one surviving instance by binding membership to a bool before asserting.
2. Add a guard so the pattern cannot return. Prefer a mechanism over vigilance: a lint rule
   (ruff/AST check in `scripts/`) that rejects `in os.environ` / `not in os.environ` directly inside
   an `assert`, or an extension of the existing fixture-repr oracle. Whichever is chosen must FAIL
   on a deliberately reintroduced instance — prove it, do not assert it.

Investigate before choosing: check whether ruff already has a rule covering this, and whether an
AST check belongs alongside the project's existing `scripts/check_*` gates rather than as a new
mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `tests/unit/test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup_heldout.py:232` no longer renders `os.environ` on
      failure — demonstrated by forcing that assertion to fail and showing the output contains a
      bool rather than the environment.
- [x] A guard rejects the pattern, and is proven by deliberately reintroducing an instance and
      observing the guard FAIL. A guard that has never been seen to fail is not evidence.
- [x] The safe `os.environ.get(...)` assertions listed above are NOT modified — this must not become
      a churn sweep over every environment assertion in the suite.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      reports `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.

## Provenance
Discovered 2026-08-20 from the implementer's note on `illusory-patronal-giraffe`; the surviving
instance and the safe/unsafe classification were established by a direct sweep of `tests/`, not
inferred.

file_impact.reason: Line 232 asserts membership directly against os.environ, rendering the full environment on failure in the op-cert key path.

compiled_state.title: Assertion on os.environ membership dumps the whole environment into CI logs on failure
